steps.what: Review work performed, test results and actual parts used
Enter work facts in the maintenance records system {OTHER}
Copy work-order identifiers and asset details into documentation
Write the maintenance log or required work report narrative

loop.input: Technician-entered actions, measurements with units, parts, unresolved faults and work-order identifiers
loop.output: Work narrative expressing only the recorded facts
loop.check: Technician edits and checks technical meaning, units, chronology and unresolved conditions against original facts in s5
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing facts or unsafe implications cause manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Use fixed report fields first; a varied repair sequence needs prose beyond a field merge

steps.what: Verify record accuracy, technical meaning and outstanding defects
Save the work documentation in the same maintenance record

tasks.design: Configure linked work-order fields in the maintenance records system {OTHER}, then draft any actual work narrative from technician-entered facts. Keep first capture and complete technical checking with the technician; ordinary same-system saving remains unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: First capture, repeated asset metadata and narrative writing were mixed together.
tasks.enabler_now: Native records configuration and a bounded factual drafting step can address those different parts separately.
tasks.still_hard: Missing readings and unclear causes cannot be repaired by fluent prose.
tasks.human_edge: The technician knows which actions were actually performed and which defects remain.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated metadata and prose composition, with unchanged responsibility for the maintenance history.

reach.learn: Asset provenance and consistent fault descriptions

evidence.claim: MaintainX supports voice-note transcription and work-order AI features; this supports factual drafting components, not the exact geothermal workflow or time estimate.
Ultimo supports preventive plans and repair history; linked-field feasibility must be checked locally.
The labour allocation and drafting reduction are provisional model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary covers actual work-performed documentation. Routine operating measurements belong to 17950; this task captures repair actions and diagnostic test results, not a second copy of operating data.

The technician supplies actions, date, parts, measurements, units and unresolved defects in fully retained s1-s2. The planner's existing work order supplies asset ID, order ID and site. Missing fields or unreadable notes are entered manually; no clean narrative or automatic diagnostic feed is assumed.

Ten repeated metadata hours can use native links. Eight of twenty narrative hours are first prose assembly, with twelve retained for editing; all twenty-four technical verification hours remain. No new report is added where a structured log already meets the real need.

The one-hour author save is fully retained and ungated. This records work; it does not close safety permits, release equipment or send a customer report. Any such consequential action needs its own measured step before extending the design.
unknowns: Which work narratives or reports are actually required
Existing work-order links and first-capture practice
research_questions: Can the current required narrative be reconstructed faithfully from entered facts without adding capture work?

already_counted.description: Edit factual narrative and verify complete technical meaning

incremental.description: Maintain work-order field mappings and narrative restrictions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is ten repeat metadata hours plus eight composition hours, less two upkeep = 16. Cautious case: unusual repairs need all twenty narrative hours manually; linked metadata still removes ten, less two upkeep = 8. First capture and ordinary saving never receive a cut.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose and correct geothermal equipment faults

steps.what: Read geothermal equipment alarms, current readings and previous repair history
Make the geothermal equipment safe and verify isolation
Test electrical systems, instrumentation and controls to identify the malfunction
Repair or adjust the faulty geothermal components
Test the repaired state and decide whether restart is safe
Restart only the checked equipment under the approved operating conditions

tasks.design: Configure a read-only asset context view across the plant monitoring and maintenance systems {OTHER}. Keep all isolation, testing, diagnosis, repair and restart actions with the qualified technician; the view never writes control settings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reading fault context may involve switching between current alarms and historical asset records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native asset links can reduce navigation without diagnosing a fault.
tasks.still_hard: Symptoms can have interacting electrical, hydraulic and control causes.
tasks.human_edge: The technician tests hypotheses against physical conditions and stops unsafe work.
tasks.altitude: One small context-navigation reduction; repair and restart responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Signal provenance and safe diagnostic sequencing

evidence.claim: A read-only asset view may reduce navigation without replacing diagnosis; feasibility and timings are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is actual fault correction, including safe restart where the qualified technician already has that authority. If a separate operator authorises restart locally, retain that existing handoff and do not claim its labour here.

The plant monitoring system supplies asset-tagged alarms, timestamps, units and quality flags. Maintenance history is created through the actual documentation task 17955. Missing tags or absent history require manual lookup in retained s1 time; no diagnostic model or new sensor is assumed.

Of ten context hours, one is repeat screen navigation and nine remain for reading, applicability checks and missing-history follow-up. All physical and judgement steps remain. Test native asset links before custom code.

Actual repair/test documentation is explicitly priced in 17955; this design does not remove or re-create it. Restart approval binds the final tested asset state, limits and settings, not the author's ordinary record save. Any changed state requires a new check.
unknowns: Asset identifiers shared by monitoring and maintenance
Restart authority and local permit workflow
research_questions: Does a linked asset view remove any real screen switching beyond existing links?

already_counted.description: Read context and handle missing or conflicting asset history

incremental.description: Check read-only asset links after equipment changes

approvals.approved_version: s5 final tested asset state with verified isolation removal conditions, settings and operating limits; a changed state voids permission

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is one context-navigation hour less 0.3 link upkeep = 0.7. If asset IDs do not align or the view already exists, all ten context hours remain and no added view is maintained, giving zero. Physical correction and restart receive no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect and record geothermal operating data

steps.what: Check required operating readings and instrument condition
Collect actual local geothermal plant and well-field measurements
Record local measurements and observations in operating records {OTHER}
Copy already displayed monitoring values into the operating records
Check timestamps, units and unusual readings and correct recording errors
Save the checked operating readings in the same record

tasks.design: Use a native read-only export from the plant monitoring system {OTHER} into the existing operating records {OTHER}. Retain local collection, first local entry, all unusual-reading checks and the ordinary author save; no new instruments or plant-control writes are assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Values already visible in monitoring may still be copied into a separate operating log.
tasks.enabler_now: An existing export can carry values, units, timestamps and quality flags with explicit tag mappings.
tasks.still_hard: Failed instruments and physically observed conditions need technician investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises readings that disagree with the actual plant state.
tasks.altitude: Less copying of existing values; operating rounds and interpretation keep their time.

reach.learn: Tag mapping, units and stale-signal detection

evidence.claim: Read-only transfer of existing tagged values to an operating log is technically feasible; the geothermal interface and time allocation are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is actual operating data collection and recording, not repair documentation in 17955. Current human copying, rather than monitoring runtime, is the eligible baseline.

The plant monitoring system already produces asset tag, measurement tag, value, unit, timestamp and quality flag. The technician collects and first enters non-instrumented readings in s2-s3 with no reduction. Missing or incompatible exports retain manual copying; no free sensor deployment or extraction is assumed.

The twenty copy hours concern existing displayed values; ten correspond to plant tags and ten to well-field tags in this provisional case. All nineteen validation and correction hours remain. A failed import does not write guessed or stale values.
Test native export configuration first. The one-hour same-system author save stays fully retained and ungated. No alarm suppression, control adjustment or external report send is automated.
unknowns: Readable export availability and current copied tags
research_questions: Can the existing export preserve units, timestamps and signal quality for the actual operating log?

already_counted.description: Validate values and repair exceptions against physical and source readings

incremental.description: Maintain tag mappings and handle failed imports

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is twenty current copy hours less three upkeep = 17. Cautious case: plant tags are compatible but well-field exports lack usable tag metadata, retaining their ten copy hours; the ten plant-copy hours removed less three upkeep give 7. Local measurement and first capture are fully retained in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine auxiliary heating or cooling needs in extreme weather

steps.what: Verify forecast conditions, building load inputs and geothermal equipment capacity
Inspect actual equipment availability and property heating or cooling conditions
Calculate extreme-weather load and compare available heating or cooling capacity
Save the calculation in the same working sheet
Check the calculation and decide whether emergency or auxiliary systems are needed
Discuss the recommendation and operating limits with the responsible operator

tasks.design: Configure a transparent load and capacity calculator in {SPREADSHEET} from technician-verified building and equipment inputs. Keep physical inspection, model applicability checks, the auxiliary-system decision and operator discussion with the technician; no equipment is activated automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeat arithmetic can be confused with the judgement about degraded capacity and uncertain weather.
tasks.enabler_now: Validated formulas and explicit capacity tables can calculate scenarios without selecting the operational response.
tasks.still_hard: Extreme conditions, unavailable backup equipment and uncertain building loads need engineering judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The technician chooses safe margins and recognises when nominal capacity is unreliable.

ambition.what: Compare an additional forecast temperature against the same verified capacity inputs before the weather peak

tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic supports an extra weather scenario; authority to activate auxiliary plant is unchanged.

reach.task: Compare building load with available capacity
reach.learn: Capacity curves, units and uncertainty margins

evidence.claim: Transparent deterministic load calculations can support a technician's auxiliary-capacity decision; the proposed implementation and timings are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is deciding need, not purchasing backup units or starting equipment. The saved working calculation is actually used for the decision; no new report or trailing log is added.

The facilities owner supplies building load coefficients and design conditions; equipment documentation supplies capacity tables and derating factors; the technician verifies forecast temperature, availability, units and applicability in s1-s2. Manual measurement, missing-data follow-up and entry are retained there, not assumed free.

Eight of twenty arithmetic hours are applying the verified building load formula and twelve are interpolating and comparing available capacity. These are current human calculations, not existing calculator runtime. All twenty-four checking and decision hours remain, including rejecting an inapplicable model.
Try the existing calculation sheet first. The one-hour ordinary save remains fully retained and ungated; live operator discussion is not an external send or automatic activation.
unknowns: Whether load coefficients and capacity curves are current
research_questions: Do the load formula and derating tables remain valid at the property's extreme-weather conditions?

already_counted.description: Check model applicability and make the auxiliary-system decision

incremental.description: Update calculation formulas and equipment capacity tables

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is twenty arithmetic hours less two upkeep = 18. Cautious case: a bespoke derating curve needs all twelve capacity-comparison hours manually, while the verified building-load formula still removes eight arithmetic hours; less two upkeep gives 6. Inspection, decision, discussion and saving remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Diagnosis, repair and operating decisions stay with the technician. Existing recorded values, repeated work-order fields and verified calculations offer separate opportunities to reduce copying and arithmetic.
reach: Work with plant operators on data quality and extreme-weather scenarios
skills_to_grow: Validate instrument tag mappings and units
Test capacity formulas against actual equipment limits
role.ambitious_version: A geothermal technician supported by reliable operating records and transparent calculations while retaining safe physical control and judgement.
